headline: Reviewed master sign plan for the North building at 75 Cherry Street, including Cambria Hotel signs.
summary: Cityplace Partners North, LLC asked for a master sign plan at 75 Cherry Street. The Design Advisory Board recommended considering approval of one location deviation for a blade sign. Signs for future tenants would need to come back for review. The minutes do not record how the board ruled.

BURLINGTON DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 
Tuesday, November 17, 2026, 5:00 PM 
 
MINUTES 
 
 Hybrid & In Person (at 645 Pine Street) Meeting 
 
Board Members Present: Caitlin Halpert, Evan Gould (5:05 PM), Geoff Hand, Miles Waite, Chase Taylor, 
and John Stilley 
 
Board Members Absent: Sean McKenzie and Marina Loughlin 
 
Staff Members Present: Scott Gustin, Mary O’Neil, and Joseph Cava 
 
Staff Members Absent: Kirk Dressing and Matthew Clark 
 
I. Agenda 
II. Communications 
III. Minutes 
IV. Master Sign Plan 
 
1. ZP-26-499; 75 Cherry Street (FD6, Ward 3) Cityplace Partners North, LLC / Jesse Robbins   
Master Sign Plan for the North building. (Project Manager, Mary O’Neil) 
Dave Farrington and Jesse Robbins: Sworn in.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Can you tell us about this proposal?  
 
Mary O’Neil: I can supplement the information that the Design Advisory Board (DAB) reviewed 
this as required when there is a request for flexibility on location. This is relative to the blade sign 
for the horizontal and vertical articulations and the signs securement within four-feet of an entrance. 
The DAB recommended consideration for approval of the deviation.  
 
Miles Waite: As do you in your staff findings? 
 
Mary O’Neil: Yes, this is discretionary on your part. 
 
Miles Waite: Okay. 
 
Mary O’Neil: This is the only deviation they are asking for, everything else is compliant.   
 
Caitlin Halpert: Is there anything you would like to add? 
 
Dave Farrington: We went through the DAB process and there were no substantial comments, and I 
have nothing else to add.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Are there any questions or comments from members of the Board?
Geoff Hand: Can you speak to the aesthetics for the proposed signage? 
 
Dave Farrington: They will be the same and similar to what we already have on the North building. 
The entrance to the main building off Bank Street, there is channel cut lettering identifying the hotel 
and additional signage on the Cherry Street and Saint Paul Street sides of the building identifying 
residences. There will be also be smaller wall mounted signs identifying the lounge and bar off Pine 
Street. We do not have any blade signs on the South building yet. 
 
Jesse Robbins: We divided the building up so it would look like two separate buildings with two 
separate sign packages. The signage between the North and South buildings will differ; the intent is 
to have two distinct sign packages.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? 
 
Jesse Robbins: The two corner projecting signs are mounted at a forty-five degree angle.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: I have a question regarding staff interpretation and the exceptions for the directional 
signs. The conclusion was no directional signs are being proposed.  
 
Mary O’Neil: There was a newer submission from the original submission package that included 
wall mounted directional signs. In order to meet the requirements of an exemption, they had to be 
less than two square feet in area. Therefore, the applicant revised the package submittal to change 
the previous proposed wall signs to blade signs for directions for parking.  
 
Geoff Hand: Under Condition 2 for the Master Sign Plan sufficient detail on the sign location, type, 
lighting and other details are required. 
 
Mary O’Neil: Correct.  
 
Geoff Hand: I was unclear on whether there were notations on the signs for approval. 
 
Mary O’Neil: I can tell you that both the Cambria Hotel signs, canopy and projecting, are included 
under this proposal. The other signs are undefined, dependent on future tenants and where and how 
they will be mounted.    
 
Geoff Hand: So they will have to come back. 
 
Mary O’Neil: Yes, and those signs will be discounted under the Master Sign Plan. The only 
definitive ones are for the Cambria Hotel, bar, and lounge signs. 
 
Jesse Robbins: There is also a potential for the canopy signs for the commercial/retail and residential 
entrances. 
 
Mary O’Neil: And the blade signs for parking. Those have been given enough definition to be 
included.  
 
Jesse Robbins: The tenants will have some flexibility under the designed parameters.  
 
Mary O’Neil: The where and the what is what is being reviewed today.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? 
Hearing none, are there any questions or comments from members of the public attending in person 
or online? Hearing none, we will close the public hearing on this item to deliberate.
V. Adjournment 
Hearing closed at 5:20 PM.
